content:
❌ Rejected the contribution.
Comment: Sorry @Sflubaduba, can't approve this clash as-is. Formatting the calendar already presents a significant challenge for many players. The leap year problem seems quite overwhelming. Please consider simplifying your clash or converting this to a puzzle :)

"Centurial years have been excluded. Every 4th year is a sufficient definition of leap year." Not for Reverse mode it's not 😅

I finished the problem in 8min (I did time myself, but since I had some context before starting you can probably add another 1-2min to my time) with the following code:

```python
dd, month, y = input().split()
day1 = ["MO","TU","WE","TH","FR","SA","SU"].index(input()[:2].upper())
D = [31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31] [["JAN","FEB","MAR","APR","MAY","JUN","JUL","AUG","SEP","OCT","NOV","DEC"] .index(month[:3].upper())]

print("----------------------")
print("|" + y.rjust(19) + " |")
print("| " + month.ljust(19) + "|")
print("|                    |")
print("|MO TU WE TH FR SA SU|")
print("|--------------------|")

w = [["  "] * 7 for _ in range(6)]
r = 0
for i in range(1, D + (int(y) % 4 == 0 and month == "February") + 1):
    w[r][(day1 + i - 1) % 7] = "XX" if i == int(dd) else str(i).zfill(2)
    r += (day1 + i) % 7 == 0

for row in w:
    print("|" + " ".join(row) + "|")

print("----------------------")
```

The next 7min were reserved for golfing; here's what I ended up with after 15min:

```python
I=input;P=print
d,m,y=I().split()
x="MoTuWeThFrSaSu".find(I()[:2])//2
j="JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec".find(m[:3])//3
D=[31,28,31,30,31,30,31,31,30,31,30,31][j]+(j==1 and int(y)%4<1)
P("-"*22)
P(f"|{y.rjust(19)} |")
P(f"| {m.ljust(19)}|")
P(f"|{' '*20}|")
P("|MO TU WE TH FR SA SU|")
P(f"|{'-'*20}|")
w=[];exec("w+=[['  ']*7];"*6)
r=0
for i in range(1,D+1):w[r][(x+i-1)%7]="XX"if i==int(d)else str(i).zfill(2);r+=(x+i)%7==0
for r in w:P(f"|{' '.join(r)}|")
P("-"*22)
```

There's a lot more to be optimized for sure, but like @5DN1L mentioned, there isn't much time at all.

I built this puzzle specifically for reverse, shortest was a last minute change.
I expect that this will be too difficult for most people to finish in 15 minutes but that's more or less where I want it. If programmers like @5DN1L and @User123 can't finish this within 5-10 minutes then I can make any of the following changes:
    -put month and year on the same line
    -remove border
    -remove month and year from output

I usually don't write my own solution when reviewing contributions, but I guess I'll make an exception for this challenge 😆

I wrote my solution at my normal pace without specifically trying to optimise for speed. It took me 16 minutes to finish. That'd have left no time for optimisation in the Shortest mode.

My thoughts on your suggestions for making the task easier:

* Putting the month and year on the same line: For me, centering them separately would be faster than combining them and then centering the result. The player either needs to know a built-in Python method for centering or spend time calculating the required spaces manually.

What would really save time is changing the requirement from center alignment to left alignment, although the calendar would look a bit less pretty.

* Removing the border: This could save a little time, but probably not much.

* Removing the month and year from the output: This would save the most time.

* I'd suggest including a sample calendar in the write statement of the stub. That would make it easier to copy and paste the top and bottom borders and the lines around the names of the days of the week. That's what I did.

* Please specify how center alignment should work when the month name has an odd length. I had to spend some time checking whether the extra space goes on the left or the right.

* Also consider specifying that each line is 22 characters long. I had to figure that out at the beginning; not character by character, but it still took some time.

* It would also save time if the input included the number of days in the month, since otherwise the player needs to set up a dictionary or conditions to determine it. However, this would remove the challenge to handle leap years.

  Alternatives could be:
  • Provide in the input all 12 month lengths and ask the player to change February from 28 to 29 in a leap year.
  • Provide in the input all 12 month lengths, plus a separate set for leap years.
  • Include the month lengths directly in the stub.

Constraints
* Second constraint: Consider removing "greater than 0". Saying that the year is four digits long already implies this.

Cases
* Validator 7: Please remove the trailing newline from the input.

* Please include 13 case pairs in total: one for each month, plus an additional case for February in a leap year.

* When revising the cases, please also make sure every day of the week appears in at least one test and at least one validator. (Surprise, surprise: Tuesday currently doesn't appear in any of the 10 validators 😆)

* Please also make sure every "today" (XX) scenario below appears in at least one test and at least one validator (a case may cover more than one scenario):
  • is in week 1
  • is in week 2
  • is in week 3
  • is in week 4
  • is in week 5
  • is in week 6
  • is day 1
  • is the last day
  • is Monday
  • is Tuesday
  • is Wednesday
  • is Thursday
  • is Friday
  • is Saturday
  • is Sunday

Thanks.

Some preliminary thoughts:

- Definitely make this an Easy puzzle, or make the clash a lot simpler 😅 The changes you've suggested seem like a good starting point.
- Please provide the full names of all months and days somewhere.
- Shortest mode may be too much; there are quite a few parts to the code and golfing all of it will definitely take a while.

Have not looked at the cases in detail yet.
I changed it yesterday so that calculating leap years and finding the days of the month are no longer necessary. I can solve it in 4 minutes now at a steady pace.

I'll think about it if you decide to remove the border and year/month from the output (since you now provide the number of days in that month, the year/month becomes decorative).

Let's see what other reviewers think :)

No worries, I'll keep it as is until some more people try it. I was hoping by switching to ready, people would be more inclined to test it and give feedback. 
I fear it's already too easy. The task now is really just editing 8 lines of text, a far cry from the challenge I originally had in mind.

For your first point, do you mean that people won't know that in reverse mode? It doesn't affect the outcome if you do account for leap years properly, but I did leave a comment in the stub generator giving the same information. I also have the names of the months and their day counts in the same comment, so I'm hoping you just didn't notice it. I can add the day names to the comment as well and move the comment down so it is more noticeable if you think that is necessary.

I'm trying to get some decent reverse puzzles out so making this a classic puzzle is the last resort. I can make it really easy by:
giving only: the day number, the first day of the month and the amount of days in the month.
and making the output: a row with the day names and 6 calendar rows.
I would like to keep it as challenging as possible, but if it's taking you 10 minutes then it probably is too difficult.

I can turn shortest off but the way I see it, you don't really need time to golf it so long as you finish it. The result is still the same: who wrote the shortest working solution in the given time?
I haven't read @User123's comment in detail yet, but first, could @User123 please add some spaces to the third line of code? It's currently so long that it affects the page layout. Thanks.
@Sflubaduba sorry I completely missed the statement in the stub generator; must have deleted the comment when I was trying the clash out.

Two more points (my previous comment has reached the character limit anyway):

* In addition to the 12 month lengths, if they're included in the input or the stub, the names of all 12 months should be included as well.

Input
* Please format "DD", "Month" and "YYYY" as [[variables]] separately.

Thanks.

Thanks for testing it! It definitely needed to be easier.
The changes I made to make it easier:
-split the given date into three separate variables
-put the names of months, each of their day amounts, the calendar dimensions and a template calendar in the stub
-changed centre alignment to left and right alignment (should be a nice middle ground)
-give single digit dates with a leading zero

I have made the months match for each pair, with a pair for each month and 2 leap and non-leap Februaries to increase the penalty for not considering leap years. So 15 pairs total.
I changed the year constraint so that people won't question if these are valid: '0000', '-100', '1BCE', etc.
All conditions that you mentioned should be satisfied but I wouldn't be surprised if I missed something.

You haven't missed anything 👏

The changes made should make the clash easier.

I think the coverage of the revised cases looks good, and the revised stub will help players a lot! 👍

Goal
* Consider adding an illustrative example that covers the currently missing specifications (the year and month lines, the number of weeks, and the overall layout). For example,

<<Explanation of the calendar format>>
```
---------------------- Fixed
|               2026 | Right-align [[YYYY]] + a space
| May                | Left-align a space + [[Month]]
|                    | Fixed
|MO TU WE TH FR SA SU| Fixed
|--------------------| Fixed
|            XX 02 03| Week 1
|04 05 06 07 08 09 10| Week 2
|11 12 13 14 15 16 17| Week 3
|18 19 20 21 22 23 24| Week 4
|25 26 27 28 29 30 31| Week 5
|                    | Week 6
---------------------- Fixed
```

Output
* Please add "{{22}} characters per line".

Cases
* My thoughts on the case names. You don't have to change them, but I'd suggest using names that are easier for players to understand 😉

  • NYE: Consider using the full form, "New Year's Eve", as not every player may know the abbreviation.

  • 30 Days Has September: But the cases are for June? 

  • A Historic Moment: Consider adding "in January" at the end.

  • It was a national tragedy (Sflubaduba's birthday): I have absolutely no idea what this reference is.

  • The Rapture. God Told Me: Again, I have no idea what this refers to.

  • Squirrels Hate This Month: Consider changing "This Month" to "November".

  • Using It All: Are you referring to the fact that all six weeks are used? If so, there are other case pairs where this also happens. Is there anything more specific to this case pair?

  • Waste of Digital Paper: Consider adding "4 weeks only".

Thanks.

I'll revise the names, but just to explain myself:
30 Days: I named it before I included the day counts in the stub. At the time, I wanted to hint but not tell.
National Tragedy: is 9/11, but the point is that my birth was the biggest tragedy of September 2001
The Rapture: I ran out of ideas
Squirrels: There's no nuts in November (if you catch my drift)
Using It All: Is the only *pair* with a 31 day month that starts on Sunday

Thanks for your help

Thanks for the explanations 😄 Some of those references definitely make more sense now.

"Hint but not tell" is absolutely fine for some contributions. But with tasks as complex as this one, I think it's better to be as direct as possible 😉

The revised case names are all good.

Just one final small suggestion: in the Goal section, please move the phrase "with the given date DD marked XX" to the last paragraph, where it would fit better.

Thanks.
I noticed that you added the number of days in the month as an input. As a result, there's no longer a need to list the months in the stub.
Good point. I decided to bite the bullet and make it easy enough for most.
